subject: Deployment mode calibration: FastCart latency & throughput follow-up
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Elena Cruz <elena@fastcart.com>, FastCart Ops <ops@fastcart.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-23T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Deployment mode calibration: FastCart latency & throughput follow-up

Hi Elena / FastCart team —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and a proposed decision path so we can converge on the right deployment mode (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC).

Call TL;DR (what I heard)
- Primary product: checkout personalization & real-time price adjustments (low token lengths, ~20-40 tokens).
- Target p95: <= 120ms for in-checkout responses; p50 objective ~50-80ms.
- Baseline sustained QPS today: ~120 rps; peak event spikes up to ~600 rps for ~10-20 minute windows.
- Data residency: US only; no air-gapped requirement for MVP.
- Procurement ask: cost estimate + SOC2 evidence and standard SLA wording.

Proposed two-phase approach (what we recommend from experience):
1) Short hosted pilot (7–10 days): run synthetic and traffic-shadowed tests against Redwood Hosted API to validate p95 at production-like payloads and token lengths. Benefits: fastest path to measure tail latency and validate kernel/quant settings.
2) Trigger rule to move to Dedicated: if sustained peak-window QPS > 250 rps for 30+ minutes OR observed p95 on Hosted > 150ms consistently during peak windows, we recommend Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) configured for predictable concurrency and lower tail latency.

What we need from you to schedule the pilot and produce a targeted recommendation: (please attach or paste)
- 1-week QPS/time-of-day profile (CSV is great)
- Typical payload token count distribution (avg/min/max)
- Any compliance/procurement forms you want on file (I attached our standard pilot checklist and an example SLA template).

I attached: redwood-pilot-checklist.pdf and a quick template SLA. I also attached a stub for a QPS CSV for your convenience — feel free to replace with your real traffic.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Elena: confirm the point-of-contact for procurement and ops + share the QPS CSV by end of week.
- We’ll schedule a 30-min pilot kickoff once we have the data (I’m proposing Mon 9/27 or Tue 9/28 morning PT).

If your ops team prefers, we can run an initial 10-minute synthetic benchmark in the call to illustrate tail behavior.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

Vanessa — thanks for the summary and the checklist.

Attaching the QPS export from last week (see FastCart_QPS_profile.csv). Key notes from our side:
- Sustained baseline: ~110–140 rps (normal traffic windows).
- Peak bursts: up to ~600 rps (Black Friday-style promotion tests and triggered events) that last ~10–25 minutes.
- Common response size: ~25–35 tokens (median ~28).
- P95 target for the product team: <= 120ms (we can accept slightly higher during extreme promotion spikes but want to understand the trade-offs).

Procurement: looping in Sara (procurement@fastcart.com) — she’ll need an initial cost estimate and SOC2/PCI controls evidence before we spin up any long-lived reserved capacity.

Ops (cc): if you need any additional telemetry or to pull sample logs for a 10-min window, let me know which fields you need.

Happy to do the kickoff on Tue 9/28 10:00 PT if that works for your team.

Thanks,

Thanks Elena — got the CSV and noted procurement. Looping in Neha, Ben and Priyom to scope the pilot and a quick decision-rule for Dedicated.

Internal summary (for Ops/Engineering pathing):
- FastCart needs p95 <= 120ms under normal peaks. They have short bursts up to 600 rps for ~10–25m.
- Given the token lengths (~25–35) and tight p95 target, we want to validate whether hosted kernel selection + prefix caching can meet the tail latency during bursts, or whether the only realistic option is Dedicated with pre-warmed KV caches and more deterministic batch sizing.

Proposed internal plan we’ll present to FastCart at kickoff:
Phase A — Hosted pilot (3–7 days, starts immediately after kickoff):
  - Run synthetic traffic that reproduces their CSV profile (sustained baseline + burst windows).
  - Enable prefix/KV caching where applicable and instrument p50/p95/p99 per model and per route.
  - If Hosted p95 <= 140ms during bursts and p95 <= 120ms during baseline windows, continue on Hosted for MVP and revisit Dedicated if sustained traffic grows.
Phase B — Dedicated recommendation trigger:
  - If observed sustained peak-window QPS > 250 rps for 30+ minutes OR if Hosted tail latency during bursts > 150ms persistently, recommend Dedicated with the following starting configuration: 4 x A100-equivalent GPU pool, fixed concurrency slots tuned to token lengths, and aggressive prefix cache warmers. (Priyom: please confirm config details below.)

Elena, we’ll bring an estimated cost delta and expected tail latency improvements to the kickoff.

Thanks —
Vanessa

[Quoted above]

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-09-24T08:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Deployment mode calibration: FastCart latency & throughput follow-up

Internal / technical note (sharing with Elena for transparency):

Based on the CSV and the target p95, my initial recommendation:
- Start with Hosted pilot using our lowest-latency kernel profile and enable continuous batching with small max_batch_size (to preserve tail latency) and aggressive KV prefix caching for repeated contexts.
- If we hit the Dedicated trigger (sustained >250 rps for 30m OR p95 >150ms during bursts), recommend the following Dedicated baseline: 
  - Provision 4 x NVIDIA A10/A100-class nodes (depending on availability in their region).
  - Configure concurrency slots to ~120 concurrent lightweight requests (given ~30 token median) and a pre-warm policy for expected burst windows (cron-based warmers ahead of marketing events).
  - Quantization profile: bf16 mixed precision with int8 fallback for non-critical models to improve throughput where quality drop is acceptable; we’ll supply a quality regression guard for model outputs.
  - Autoscale policy: scale by target queue depth with 60s evaluation window; burst capacity to add 1–2 nodes for short spikes.

I attached a short outline (dedicated-config-outline.yaml) that includes the slot sizing and autoscaler knobs. Priyom
